decisions.decision: ANALYSIS RECORDED (no tickets minted — human chose analysis-only for now): LOOP ENGINEERING / GOAL-DRIVEN AUTONOMY is compatible with this framework. Same-session self-paced loops (/loop + ScheduleWakeup, autonomous-loop sentinels) are SAFE NOW — one orchestrator thread, no state race; this is exactly how 'proceed until the end' epics already run. The ONE real crash mode is CONCURRENT STATE WRITERS from CronCreate cloud routines firing while a local orchestrator session is active (two writers on state/ + tasks/ + index.json); the pointer's active_session_id is advisory — nothing enforces mutual exclusion. The framework is actually well-suited to looping: state survives context resets via the bundle+RESUME-FIRST design, tickets-with-ACs ARE goal units (list_ready/index.json = work queue + termination signal), and dev->reviewer is a bounded self-correcting inner loop. An autonomous loop MUST hard-stop at the four human gates: destructive/irreversible ops, UAT verdicts (uat-only cannot self-satisfy its done-gate), genuinely ambiguous scope, and release/version-bump/push. RECOMMENDATION (deferred): Tier1 = codify the stop-gates into the orchestrator-routing skill (zero code); Tier2 = single-active-session advisory lock (pid+heartbeat in the pointer or state/.lock) so cron routines refuse to start when another orchestrator holds the repo (closes the only crash mode); Tier3 = define a 'goal' as an epic-label over tickets, loop drains list_ready for that label until empty or a gate fires.
